etymologies.etymologyHTML: Corresponding to learn +‎ -ing, from Middle English lerninge, used in all modern senses (act of learning; accumulated knowledge; thing learned).

definitions.definition: (uncountable) An act in which something is learned.
(countable, proscribed) Something that has been learned.

quote.citation: 2007 April 5, Stuart Elliott, “Online Experiment for Print Magazine”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: “We’ll take the learnings and apply them to the rest of our business.”

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of learn

quote.citation: 2024 May 4, Mat Gallagher, “I tried Mercedes’ new autonomous driving in busy city streets – it's mind-blowing”, in T3‎[2]:
quote.text: The system is still learning though, and will improve how it handles situations thanks to crowd-sourced data from across the Mercedes network.
